appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.contrastNote: The number next to a background is the contrast of the text on it: from 4.5 it reads well (WCAG AA), under 3 badly. Next to the warning icons it is their contrast on a tile: from 3 they stand out.
appearance.hexBad: {token}: “{value}” is not a colour. Write it as #rrggbb or #rgb, the # may be left out; Escape puts the colour back.
appearance.name: Name

help.theme: Light or dark, or as the system: the page then follows the device's setting and changes with it.
help.blink: Whether the triangle of a warning and the cross of a failure blink, so that they are not missed: always, for the first five seconds a sign is shown, or never. As the system blinks unless the device asks for reduced motion.
help.iconWindow: How an open window is drawn, in a room's head and its lists, with the triangle of a warning and the cross of a failure: the opening sash, its mark inside its frame, or the paned window of the original MAX! software, its mark at the bottom right. A window contact's icon follows.
help.iconRadio: How a radio fault is drawn, a device that lost its link or that the Cube could not reach: the Wi-Fi fan, or the tower of the thermostats' display. Its mark is at the bottom right.
help.scheme: The page's colours, as a light and a dark set; the mode picks which is shown. Customise… edits a copy of the chosen scheme, Save as keeps it in this browser under a name, Export saves it as a file and Import reads such a file.
sysinfo.install.other: Other: by hand, a container or another supervisor
sysinfo.apiAll: The web interface listens on all of them, port {port}.
sysinfo.proxyPlain: none, plain HTTP at the proxy
sysinfo.proxyHint: The server does not trust this proxy: named with -trusted-proxies, it shows the proxy's address and certificate here.
sysinfo.proxyNoScheme: The proxy sends no X-Forwarded-Proto: with it, the server reads the proxy's certificate.
update.title: Software update
update.flavour.nightly: nightly: the newest tested change, each night
update.channelHint: A channel takes its own releases and those of every more stable one: devel, nightly, alpha, beta, rc, stable.
update.channelApt: apt follows the suite {channel}; choose another channel, and the next update switches it.
update.channelAptSwitch: apt follows the suite {suite}; the next update switches it to {channel}, and installs a release of {channel} once one is newer than the one installed: nothing is downgraded.
update.channelBrew: Homebrew follows the formula {formula}: to follow another channel, uninstall it and install that channel's formula.
update.channelVariable: MASSIMO_UPDATE_CHANNEL sets the channel {channel}; a choice here applies once it is removed.
update.noRelease: No release on this channel yet.
update.blocked: Updating from here is not possible: {reason}.
update.cannotAsk: Cannot ask the server about updates: {error}
update.confirm: Install {version} and restart the server? It is offline for a short while; if the new version does not come up, the old one is put back.
update.confirmManaged: Install {version} through {manager} and restart the server? It is offline for a short while; if the new version does not come up, nothing is undone, and the last update says how to go back.
restart.confirm: Restart the server? It is offline for a few seconds; open pages reconnect by themselves.
restart.notBack: The server has not come back within two minutes; look at its service on the box.
restart.cannotAsk: Cannot ask the server about the restart: {error}
reboot.confirm.one: Reboot the computer in {n} second? Every service on it stops for a while; if it does not come back, someone has to go to it.
reboot.confirm.other: Reboot the computer in {n} seconds? Every service on it stops for a while; if it does not come back, someone has to go to it.
reboot.confirmNow: Reboot the computer now? Every service on it stops for a while; if it does not come back, someone has to go to it.
reboot.back: The computer is back; the server started {time}.
reboot.notBack: The server has not come back within five minutes; someone may have to go to the computer.
reboot.cannotAsk: Cannot ask the server about the reboot: {error}
reboot.badDelay: The delay is a whole number of seconds from 0 to {max}.
maint.title: Maintenance
maint.restartText: The service manager starts the server again; it is offline for a few seconds, and open pages reconnect by themselves.
maint.rebootText: Every service on the computer stops with the server for a while; the thermostats keep their programmes, and the page reconnects once it is back.
maint.announceHint: By mDNS, for massimo discover, the apps and Home Assistant. Automatic is on unless the server listens on the loopback, as behind a reverse proxy; a change applies at the next restart.
maint.announceNowOff: The server does not announce itself now.
maint.announceWaits: The change waits for the next restart.
maint.announceFixed: Set by {by}, which wins over this choice.
maint.announceSaved: Saved: it applies at the next restart.
maint.pollHint: How often the server asks each Cube for its device list: what the thermostats, windows and batteries last reported. The Cube answers from its memory, so a poll costs no radio time; a Cube that leaves two polls in a row unanswered counts as lost.
maint.refreshHint: How often the server connects to each Cube anew and reads everything the Cube holds: the devices' settings, the rooms, its radio budget. It catches a change the Cube took but did not apply. Off: only at the start and after a lost connection.
maint.discoverHint: How often the server looks for Cubes on the LAN: a new Cube, or one that moved to another address. Off: only on request, or while a Cube has to be found.
maint.dutyWait: Re-read the radio budget after a hold every
maint.dutyWaitHint: When the Cube's radio duty cycle is used up, radio commands wait: this long, then the server reads the Cube's budget again, at no radio cost, and sends them once it has fallen. The duty cycle falls within the hour, so the server does not wait for the next full hour.
maint.intervalWaits: The change waits for the next restart; this run: {value}.
maint.intervalFixed: Set by {by} for this run, which wins over this choice: {value}.
maint.intervalSaved: Saved: it applies at the next restart.
maint.fileText: The server reads {file} again by itself within ten seconds of a change; Reload now reads it at once, as SIGHUP does, and checkpoints the store.
maint.cfgVars: Variables, with where each came from:
help.title: What does this do?
help.profileName: The name the personal page and the users list show; your login name stays as it is. Save keeps it.
help.profilePassword: A password lets you sign in by your name in any browser. It is registered by OPAQUE in this browser, so the server never sees it; a change asks for the current one. Save sets it.
help.profileTokens: Each browser signed in as you is a session; an API key signs in a program. Revoke ends one at once, signing that browser or program out. Create key makes a key, shown only once: copy it then.
help.profileLinked: Link signs you in once at the provider; the account that comes back is shown, and Link there makes it sign you in here too. Linking again at a provider replaces the link there. Remove ends a link, but not your last way to sign in.
help.roomName: The room's name, stored on the Cube and shown by every program that talks to it.
help.comfort: The comfort temperature (sun symbol), 21.0 °C from the factory. The thermostats switch to it with their comfort/eco button.
help.eco: The eco or set-back temperature (moon symbol), for nights and absences, 17.0 °C from the factory. The thermostats switch to it with their comfort/eco button.
help.windowTemp: The temperature the radiator thermostats set while a window is open, 12 °C from the factory. A window contact in the room reports the opening as it happens; without one, a radiator thermostat detects it from a sharp fall in temperature.
help.windowMinutes: How long a radiator thermostat keeps the open-window temperature after it detected an open window itself from a sharp fall in temperature, 15 minutes from the factory; 0 switches this detection off. With a window contact in the room the thermostats ignore temperature falls and keep the open-window temperature until the window is closed.
help.maxTemp: The highest temperature that can be set on the thermostats of the room.
help.minTemp: The lowest temperature that can be set on the thermostats of the room.
help.boostMinutes: How long Boost, started with the Boost button on a thermostat, keeps the valve open: 0 to 30 minutes in steps of 5, or 60; 5 minutes from the factory. Afterwards the thermostat returns to its previous mode and temperature.
help.boostValve: How far the valve opens during Boost, 80 % from the factory.
help.decalc: Once a week the radiator thermostats open and close their valves once so that they do not calcify (descaling run); meanwhile they show “CAL” and cannot be operated. The day and hour of that run, Saturday at 12:00 from the factory.
help.maxValve: The furthest the radiator thermostats open the valve, 100 % from the factory; lower it if a radiator heats too strongly when fully open.
help.valveOffset: A percentage the radiator thermostats add to every valve position they compute while regulating. 0 % from the factory; change it only for a valve that needs it.
help.deviceName: The device's name, stored on the Cube.
help.tempOffset: Corrects the temperature this thermostat measures, from −3.5 to +3.5 °C, since the temperature next to the radiator can differ from the rest of the room. Example: set to 20 °C, but the room only reaches 18 °C: an offset of −2.0 °C. In a room with a wall thermostat the temperature is measured at the wall thermostat.
help.displayActual: The wall thermostat's display shows the measured room temperature instead of the set temperature.
help.deviceRoom: Moves the device to another room; it is then linked with the thermostats of that room and follows its settings.
help.onlyDay: On: changes apply to the edited day only. Off: changes apply to every selected day at once, the days that have the same programme.
help.poll: How often the page asks the server for the Cube's state. Changes reported by the devices arrive in between as they happen.
help.expert: Shows radio addresses, device types, the Cube's radio budget and the server version.
help.clock: The Cube keeps its own time zone. Show its clock converted to the browser's time zone, or as the Cube has it.
help.language: The language of this page. From the browser follows the browser's preferred languages; a text without a translation is shown in English.

link.held: The connection is lost; the server holds it open until {time}, so that it carries on when the network is back.
link.stale: The Cube answers on the network but refuses the server: it still holds the server's old connection, as after an outage of the server's network. It lets go after up to about 40 minutes; a reboot frees it at once.
link.busy: The Cube answers on the network but refuses the server: another client holds it, such as the MAX! software, another server or an integration.

cubes.flagNote: Served for this run only, from serve's command line (-addr or -sn); it is not in the server's store and cannot be changed here.

cubes.slotsFull: The Cube's memory slots stay full ({slots} free) with nothing of the server's on its way: they hold radiograms for devices that do not answer, and radio commands wait for free slots. Reboot the Cube, below, to drop them; it is the owner's to do.
cubes.slotsLow: Few of the Cube's memory slots are free ({slots}) with nothing of the server's on its way: they hold radiograms for devices that do not answer, and radio commands wait for free slots. Reboot the Cube, below, to drop them; it is the owner's to do.
cubes.otherNetwork: {address} lies outside the networks of this machine: the server reaches it only through a router.
cubes.otherNetworkFix: A Cube without a DHCP lease uses 192.168.0.222. Check the router's DHCP and restart the Cube, or give it a fixed address in this machine's network:
cubes.changedMeanwhile: Changed meanwhile on the server, now: {value}. Save keeps yours.
pairing.how: Start puts the Cube into pairing mode. Then press the pairing button of the new device, as its manual says; each device that joins is listed here.
pairing.left: Pairing: {seconds} s left. Press the device's pairing button now.
pairing.copied: The room's settings were copied, the week programme for {days} of 7 days.
pairing.modeNotSet: The Cube did not take the switch to AUTO; the device keeps its mode.
pairing.noRooms: The Cube has no room to put the device into.
help.cubes: The Cubes this server serves, kept in its store. A change applies at once: a new address reconnects, a new proxy address restarts that proxy, and hidden devices leave the tiles, the API and the original software. The settings file's lines only add a Cube the server does not know yet; where one differs from what is set here, the Cube says so and offers the file's value.
help.providers: Users sign in through an OpenID Connect provider such as Nextcloud, Google or Microsoft, beside their password. Register this server at the provider as a client with the redirect URI shown, then add the provider here with its issuer, client ID and secret. A provider may create the users who sign in, with a role and their e-mail domains; otherwise a user links the provider's account on the personal page.
help.integrations: Programs such as Home Assistant act here for their users. With the switch on, an integration may ask to be registered without a key: compare the code it shows with the one here, then approve it with the most it may do. A registered integration acts as its own user, or as the Massimo user you link it to; Revoke takes its key away.

repair.title: Repairs
repair.costRadio: Radiograms: {radiograms} · duty cycle: about {duty} % · memory slots: {slots}, {held} of them until the devices' next wakeup · wakeups: {wakeups}
repair.costMetadata: No radio cost: only the Cube's room and device list is written.
repair.costResets: No radio cost: resets: {n}, the Cube's bookkeeping.
repair.done: Sent: the Cube accepted {accepted} of {lines} lines.
repair.stillFlagged: The Cube's device list still shows a communication error for {devices}.
repair.cleared: The Cube's device list shows no communication error for them any more.
repair.roomName: Room {room} is not in the Cube's list; its name
repair.deviceName: The device is not in the Cube's list; its name
repair.resetHelp: Clears the Cube's communication error of every device of the Cube that has one: one reset each, at no radio cost.
repair.roomResetHelp: Clears the Cube's communication error of the room's devices that have one: one reset each, at no radio cost.
repair.masterHelp: Where the Cube's list names no thermostat of the room as its master, names its wall thermostat, else its first radiator thermostat. No radio.
repair.relinkHelp: Sends every device of the room its links with the others and its room again, adding only: nothing is unlinked.
repair.unlinkRelinkHelp: Removes every link between the room's devices, then builds them again. For a room whose links a re-link did not mend; not yet tried on hardware.
repair.unlinkRelinkWarning: Warning: every link of the room is removed before it is built again: {cost}. This has not yet run on real hardware. A run that stops halfway, at a radiogram the Cube refuses or a lost connection, leaves the room's devices without their partners: the room's setpoints and the wheel turns no longer reach every device until it is run again.
repair.unlinkRelinkConfirm: Unlink every link of this room and re-link it now?
repair.configHelp: Sends the device the temperatures and the week programme that most of the room's other thermostats share, where its own differ.
repair.placeHelp: Moves the device by radio into the room the Cube's list has it in, where the Cube has it in another room or in none.
repair.list: List where the Cube has it
repair.listHelp: Moves the device in the Cube's list to the room the Cube has it in. No radio.
cap.passwords: set users' passwords, not an owner's
cap.cubes.reboot: reboot a Cube, which drops the radiograms it has not delivered
cap.reboot: reboot the computer the server runs on
cap.integrations: register integrations and link their users
help.users: Everyone who signs in has one role, which says what they may do. A guest has an end date; a user without a password signs in with keys only. A password set here ends the user's sessions.
help.roles: A role is a set of capabilities, each guarding part of what the page and the API do. The six default roles can be renamed and reshaped, except the owner; more can be created. A disabled role keeps its users out.
help.capabilities: A capability switched off here is denied to every role but the owner, whatever the roles say: for example pairing while nobody should pair, or updates on a box updated by hand.
help.pairCopy: Gives the device the settings of the room's first other thermostat, as the original software does: the temperatures go to every thermostat of the room, the valve settings and the week programme to the device. It costs radio budget: about a tenth of an hour's for the temperatures and the valve settings, and 8 % for each day of the programme that differs, so up to two thirds for a new thermostat. Switched off, the device keeps its own settings.
backup.title: Backup and restore
help.backup: A backup holds the Cube's rooms, names, device settings and week programmes. Download backup saves the Cube as it is now. The server keeps backups too: after a change, by hand and before every restore. Restore… shows what it would send before anything is sent.
backup.noHistory: This Cube is not in the server's store, so the server keeps no backups of it.
backup.same: Same configuration as the one before.
restore.nothing: The Cube already holds this backup: nothing to send.
restore.cost: {n} radio commands, about {pct} % of the hourly radio budget; the Cube is at {now} %.
connect.noBridge: This page belongs to the Massimo app for Android and iOS. In a browser, Massimo is the web UI at the server's address.

connect.unreachable: {name} does not answer at its addresses.
connect.foundNone: No server found that is not in the list yet.
connect.addressHint: A name or an address, with its port where it is not the usual one, or the whole URL.
connect.plainHttp: Not encrypted: outside the home network, anyone on the way can read the sign-in and change the page.
connect.badAddress: That is not an address: write a name, an address with its port, or a URL such as https://massimo.example.net/.

connect.remoteHint: The address from outside, such as https://massimo.example.net/; empty for none.
connect.biometric: Ask for my fingerprint or PIN
connect.biometricHint: The phone asks for it before the app signs in to this server.
connect.badURL: An address is a URL, such as https://192.168.1.20:8099/.
connect.noAddress: A server needs at least one address.
connect.removeQuestion: Remove {name} from the app, with its sign-in?
connect.fpText: The server at {address} has a certificate of its own, which the phone cannot check by itself. Trust it only if its fingerprint is the server's.
connect.fpChangedText: The server at {address} shows another certificate than the one trusted until now. The server may have made a new one, or someone is in between. Trust the new one only if its fingerprint is the server's.
connect.fpCompare: Compare it with the fingerprint in the server's log, or with massimo tls show on the box, before you trust it.
connect.core: Run the server on this phone
connect.coreText: The phone then talks to the Cube itself. A Cube takes one connection at a time: while the phone holds it, nothing else reaches that Cube directly.
